newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares grounded by Vienna airport.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares grounded by Vienna airport.

text.p: Austrian shares ended flat on Wednesday after a brief test of support and traders forecast the ATX index would remain pinned in a narrow range over the next few days.
The ATX index of 21 blue-chip shares closed 1.03 points down at 1,080.11, a shade above support at 1,080 and off a session low of 1,077.34. Nine issues were up, 10 down and two unchanged.
"I see the market back in a narrow trading range of plus/minus one or two points," said a trader, adding that a weaker German bond market had dampened sentiment.
Selling pressure on Vienna airport company Flughafen Wien and high-grade steelmaker Boehler-Uddeholm more than offset demand for engineering group VA Tech and steel firm VA Stahl.
Flughafen was the biggest percentage decliner, dipping 2.18 percent, or 11 schillings, to 494. Traders traced the decline to one sizeable selling order.
Boehler-Uddeholm, which reported a 22 percent drop in nine-month net profit on Tuesday, slipped 13 schillings to 740 on brisk turnover of 22,465 lots.
VA Tech was the most actively traded share and among the session's main gainers. It added on 20 schillings to 1,620 on turnover of 24,912 lots.
Industrial group Radex-Heraklith was the top percentage gainer, rising 2.1 percent, or 6.5 schillings to 315.5.
The broad-based Vienna bourse index eased 0.62 points to 413.74. December ATX futures stood 0.9 points down at 1,082. -- Vienna Newsroom, 43-1-53112-258
